Optik derinlik dalga boyuna bağlıdır; gö: Optical depth depends on wavelength; a cloud that is thick in the visible spectrum can be nearly transparent in microwave.
Optik özellikleri belirleyen LWC ile dam: What determines optical properties is the effective radius given jointly by LWC and droplet concentration. When the same LWC is partitioned into numerous small droplets, the cloud becomes brighter and longer-lived.

Shortwaves (storm systems) propagate eastward, while longwaves (blockings) remain in place for weeks; the interaction between the two constitutes the difficulty of weekly forecasting.
Orta enlem kışında EP akısı tipik olarak: In mid-latitude winter, the EP flux is typically directed upward and equatorward; the jet streak is continuously fed by this wave flux.

Orta enlem siklonunun kapalı dolaşım hal: The closed circulation ring of a mid-latitude cyclone has a radius of 300–800 km.
Orta enlem sinoptik sistemleri için tipi: Typical scales are chosen for mid-latitude synoptic systems: horizontal velocity U ~ 10 m/s, length L ~ 10⁶ m, vertical velocity W ~ 10⁻² m/s, pressure perturbation δp ~ 10³ Pa, density 1 kg/m³, f ~ 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹, a ~ 6×10⁶ m, time scale L/U ~ 10⁵ s (one day).
Orta enlem sinoptik ölçekte (L ≈ 1000 km: At the mid-latitude synoptic scale (L ≈ 1000 km, U ≈ 10 m/s), the pressure gradient force and the Coriolis force are of the same order of magnitude; the acceleration term is an order of magnitude smaller. This is precisely where the geostrophic approximation originates.
Orta enlem yağmurunun büyük kısmı erimiş: Most mid-latitude rain is melted snow: the Bergeron process grows crystals to mm size in the −10…−20 °C layer, and they melt as they fall past 0 °C. Cloud seeding (silver iodide) triggers this process: it provides the missing ice nuclei.
Orta enlem, kutup soğuk havası ile tropi: Because the mid-latitudes are the belt where polar cold air meets tropical warm air, they are baroclinic by nature. The thermal wind is nonzero, a jet stream exists, and systems tilt westward with height.
Orta enlemde 1,6·10⁻¹¹ m⁻¹s⁻¹; ekvatorda: 1.6·10⁻¹¹ m⁻¹s⁻¹ at mid-latitudes; maximum at the equator, zero at the poles.
Orta enlemde 10 m/s kuzey rüzgârı: fv =: Northerly wind of 10 m/s at mid-latitudes: fv = 10⁻⁴ × 10 = 10⁻³ m/s² eastward acceleration. The velocity turns 90° in 6 hours.
Orta enlemde 10 m/s rüzgâr için Coriolis: Coriolis acceleration for a 10 m/s wind at mid-latitudes is 2·7.29×10⁻⁵·10·sin45° ≈ 1.0×10⁻³ m/s²: it appears small, but turns the velocity by 90° in 6 hours (inertia circle).
Orta enlemde 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; kuzeye giden hava: 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ at mid-latitudes; northward-moving air gains more f, its relative vorticity decreases, and it turns anticyclonically.
Orta enlemde 500 km'lik bir kutuda f yak: In a 500 km box at mid-latitudes, f varies by about 5%; the f-plane is a defensible approximation at this scale.
Orta enlemde R = 500 km için Dünya payı: For R = 500 km at mid-latitudes, the Earth's contribution is 1.15·10⁷ m²/s; the air's contribution (at 20 m/s) is 10⁷ m²/s — both are of the same order of magnitude.

Parsel çevreden sıcakken birim kütle baş: The work gained per unit mass while the parcel is warmer than the environment; twice the square root of it is the storm's updraft speed.
Parsel δs kadar yol alırken teğet birim: The angle swept by the unit tangent vector as the parcel travels a distance δs. It is the angle variable of the δs = R δψ relation between arc length and radius of curvature, measured in radians.

Parsele verilen ısı (J, birim kütle başı: Heat added to the parcel (J, per unit mass, W/kg) increases internal energy and performs expansion work. For dry air, c_v, c_p and α = RT/p.
Parseli izleyen değişim, sabit noktadaki: The rate of change following the parcel is the sum of the local rate of change at a fixed point and the advection transported by the wind. In exams, it is often inverted: the local rate of change at the station is ∂ψ/∂t = Dψ/Dt − V·∇ψ.
Parseli izleyen yoğunluk değişimi; sürek: Density change following the parcel; the term in the Lagrangian form of the continuity equation. Equal to the negative of divergence multiplied by density.
Parseli −10 °C'nin altına çıkar: karışık: Lift the parcel below −10 °C: mixed-phase region.
Parselin dönen Dünya'ya göre hızı; meteo: Velocity of the parcel relative to the rotating Earth; this is the quantity directly measured by meteorological observations. It remains small compared to the frame velocity, but is the sole term that governs atmospheric motion.
Parselin eylemsiz çerçevedeki hızı: bağı: Velocity of the parcel in the inertial frame: vector sum of the relative wind and the Earth's frame velocity. The law of momentum is formulated directly in terms of this velocity.
Parselin izlediği basınç değerinin madde: Material derivative of the pressure tracked by the parcel, that is, vertical velocity in pressure coordinates. Its sign is opposite to geometric vertical velocity because pressure decreases with height.
Parselin konumu zamanla ilerler; hız ala: The position of the parcel advances with time; meanwhile, the velocity field may also change. In steady flow (∂V/∂t = 0), the right-hand side is identical to that of the streamline → trajectory = streamline = streakline. Otherwise, the three diverge.
Parselin konumunun zamana göre türevi, t: The time derivative of the parcel's position is, by definition, the parcel's velocity. Since the parcel moves along with the air, this velocity is the wind itself.

Parselin θ'sı başlangıç seviyesindeki çe: The parcel's θ remains equal to the environmental θ at the initial level; environmental θ has changed by ∂θ/∂z δz. If ∂θ/∂z > 0, restoring force: harmonic oscillation equation.
Parçacık animasyonu bugün en çok tanınan: Particle animation is the most widely recognized representation today. Its logic consists of three parts: (1) thousands of particles are scattered at random positions, (2) in each frame, each particle is advected one step along the field, (3) instead of clearing the canvas completely, it is slightly dimmed; thus, old positions leave a fading **streak trail**. On top of this, a **lifetime** is added: each particle dies after a certain number of frames and is reborn at a random location.
Parçacık boyutu dalga boyuyla karşılaştı: Scattering weakly dependent on wavelength and predominantly forward-directed, occurring when particle size is comparable to wavelength.
Parçacık büyürse (toz, damlacık): Mie re: If the particle grows (dust, droplet): transition to the Mie regime occurs, and scattering becomes almost insensitive to wavelength → the cloud appears WHITE.
Parçacık dalga boyundan çok küçük olmalı: The particle must be much smaller than the wavelength (x ≪ 0,1).
Parçacık izi rüzgârın ESTİĞİ yönü göster: The particle trail shows the direction the wind BLOWS TO; the meteorological direction expression ("north wind") is the direction it COMES FROM.
Parçacık küresel ve homojen kabul edilir: The particle is assumed to be spherical and homogeneous.
Parçacıkların sıkıştığı yer akışın hızla: Where particles converge is where the flow accelerates (convergence/jet entrance).
Parçacıkların yönünü takip et; nereden n: Follow the direction of the particles; from where to where?
Parçaların hepsi hazırdı; birleştirince: All the pieces were ready; combining them yields the radial equation.
Patlayıcı gelişim genelde kış aylarında,: Explosive development is typically observed in winter, over warm ocean currents, and in the left-exit region of a strong jet. Heat and moisture fluxes from the sea surface destabilize the lower layer, latent heat release strengthens ascent, and combined with upper-level divergence, the deepening becomes self-sustaining.

Pay, bir paketi yerine geri iten kaldırm: The numerator is the strength of the buoyancy force pushing a parcel back to its position (the square of the Brunt-Väisälä frequency). The denominator represents the rate at which vertical shear extracts turbulent kinetic energy from the flow. If the ratio is small, shear wins and the flow mixes.
Pay, iki değişkenin ortalamalarından sap: The numerator sums whether the deviations of two variables from their means covary (covariance). The denominator removes units by dividing this sum by each variable's own variability. The result is dimensionless: measuring temperature in °C or K does not change r.
Paydada toplam basınç değil kuru hava ba: The denominator contains the dry air pressure (p − e), not the total pressure. This detail distinguishes w from q and makes w conserved: as the parcel ascends, since both the dry air mass and water vapor mass remain constant, their ratio also remains constant. Until condensation begins, w is the parcel's invariant label.
Paydadaki 2'yi terim terim dağıt: Distribute the 2 in the denominator term by term
Paydadaki r_s/r_a oranı bitkinin denetim: The r_s/r_a ratio in the denominator carries the plant's control. r_a is aerodynamic resistance: it decreases as wind increases, facilitating evaporation. r_s is surface (stomatal) resistance: if the plant is under water stress, it closes its stomata, r_s increases, and transpiration decreases. Therefore, under identical weather conditions, an irrigated field and an arid field produce very different ET.
Paydadaki yüzey ısı akısı pozitifse (gün: If the surface heat flux in the denominator is positive (daytime heating), L becomes negative: unstable conditions.
Paydayı sadeleştir: q = ε e / (p − e + ε: Simplify the denominator: q = ε e / (p − e + ε e).
Paylaşımın nasıl yapıldığı yüzey tipine: How the partitioning occurs depends on the surface type. Over wet and vegetated surfaces, most of the energy goes into evaporation as LE and the surface remains cool; over dry surfaces, H dominates, the air heats rapidly, and the mixing layer deepens.
Paylaşımın oranı yüzeyin nemliliğine bağ: The partitioning ratio depends on surface moisture and is measured by the Bowen ratio. Over a wet surface, most of the energy goes into LE and the temperature increase remains limited; over an arid surface, H dominates and the air warms rapidly. Therefore, irrigation can lower the local maximum temperature by several degrees.

For thin cirrus, radiation from the warm surface below mixes in, and T_b appears higher than the true cloud-top temperature.

Thus, the surface temperature, which is difficult to measure, is eliminated from the equation.

Planck eğrisi tek bir sıcaklıkla tamamen: The Planck curve is completely determined by a single temperature: if you know the temperature, you know the entire spectrum, and vice versa. All temperature retrieval in satellite meteorology is built upon this inversion.
Planck fonksiyonu, radyasyon teorisinin: The Planck function is the starting point of radiation theory: the Stefan–Boltzmann law is its integral, and Wien's law is its peak. The form directly used in meteorology is its inversion — a satellite measures radiance in a channel, and by inverting the function, the brightness temperature Tb is obtained.
Planck fonksiyonunu tüm dalga boylarına: Integrate the Planck function over all wavelengths: E = π∫Bλ(T) dλ.
Planck yasası siyah cisim içindir; gerçe: Planck's law is for a blackbody; if the emissivity of the real surface is not 1, the measured temperature turns out lower than the true temperature.

Planeter dalga sayısı n, bir enlem çembe: The planetary wavenumber n counts how many full waves fit into a latitude circle and is an integer — because the circle is closed. In mid-latitudes, n = 3–7 is the typical longwave regime; n = 1–2 indicates strong blocking, while n > 8 represents an active regime full of shortwaves.
Planeter vortisite adveksiyonu: meridyon: Planetary vorticity advection: meridional motion altering relative vorticity through the variation of f. This is the restoring term of the Rossby wave.
Planeter vortisite: Dünya'nın dönüşünün: Planetary vorticity: projection of Earth's rotation onto the local vertical axis. It is the Coriolis parameter in the equation of motion, and the inherited rotation of the air in the vorticity equation.
Planeter vortisitenin enlemle değişmesin: Large-scale atmospheric waves propagating westward, arising from the latitudinal variation of planetary vorticity.

Poisson denklemi: θ = T·(p₀/p)^κ. Havanı: Poisson equation: θ = T·(p₀/p)^κ. The temperature air would attain if brought dry-adiabatically down to 1000 hPa.
Polar cephe kuşağında ∂T/∂y ≈ 1 K/100 km: In the polar frontal zone ∂T/∂y ≈ 1 K/100 km · frontal zone at 500 hPa 5–10 K/500 km
Polar jet güçlü biçimde dalgalıdır; genl: The polar jet is strongly wavy; when its amplitude grows, cold air is transported south and warm air north. This undulation is why cold and warm spells in mid-latitudes are two sides of the same pattern.
Polar jet ile kutup girdabı karıştırılır: The polar jet is often confused with the polar vortex; the vortex is a broad circulation structure in the stratosphere, while the jet is a narrow ribbon of flow at the top of the troposphere.
Polar jetten daha yüksektedir (12–16 km): It is higher than the polar jet (12–16 km) and generally weaker, but in winter it can exceed 100 m/s over East Asia. The two jets sometimes merge; the confluence zone creates a very strong baroclinic zone and sets the stage for explosive cyclogenesis.
Potansiyel (konvektif) kararsızlık ayrı: Potential (convective) instability is a distinct concept and examines the θe profile: even if the layer itself is initially stable, it can become unstable when lifted as a whole. Layers that are moist at lower levels and dry at upper levels exhibit this behavior.
Potansiyel ET, su kısıtı olmasaydı gerçe: Potential ET is the evapotranspiration that would occur without water limitations; actual ET is constrained by soil moisture. The difference between the two is an indicator of drought.
Standard in the definition of potential temperature.
Potansiyel sıcaklık, bir hava parselini: Potential temperature is the temperature an air parcel would have if brought dry-adiabatically to 1000 hPa; it is CONSERVED in adiabatic motions.
Potansiyel sıcaklık, hava parselini adya: Potential temperature is the temperature you would measure when you bring an air parcel adiabatically to 1000 hPa. It is conserved in a dry adiabatic process, which is why it is much more useful than temperature for tracking air masses.
Potansiyel sıcaklığın logaritması entrop: The logarithm of potential temperature is entropy itself; therefore, an enclosed area on a thermodynamic diagram corresponds directly to energy.
PowerShell’de çalıştırılır; dağıtımı ind: Run in PowerShell; downloads and installs the distribution. Done once.
Pozitif F frontogenez (cephe keskinleşiy: Positive F means frontogenesis (front is sharpening), negative F means frontolysis (front is decaying). Three mechanisms contribute: deformation, convergence, and vertical motion tilting sloping layers.
Pozitif gölge (sıcak advekasyon) genelde: Positive shading (warm advection) generally goes with isentropic ascent, clouds, and precipitation; negative shading (cold advection) goes with clearing and unstable cumulus.
Pozitif vortisite advekasyonu (PVA) — ya: Positive vorticity advection (PVA) — that is, AHEAD of the vorticity maximum — produces upper-level divergence and ascent; deepening of surface low pressure typically occurs there.
Pozitif vortisite adveksiyonu (PVA), yük: Positive vorticity advection (PVA) means the transport of high-vorticity air into a region of lower vorticity and produces ascent. Not the vorticity maximum itself, but the area IN FRONT OF it is important; development occurs there. The most practical way to track shortwaves is to follow vorticity maxima.
Pozitif ζ kuzey yarım kürede siklonik, g: Positive ζ corresponds to cyclonic rotation in the Northern Hemisphere and anticyclonic rotation in the Southern Hemisphere.
Pozitif: hava yayılıyor (üst seviye jet: Positive: air is diverging (upper-level jet exit, surface anticyclone); negative: converging (surface low).
Pozitifliği şart olan alanlar (nem, yağı: Fields where positivity is required (moisture, precipitation, pollutant)
Pozitifse hacimden hava çıkıyor (diverja: If positive, air is exiting the volume (divergence); if negative, it is filling in (convergence).
Pozitifse hava dağılıyor (ıraksama), neg: If positive, air is dispersing (divergence); if negative, it is gathering (convergence).
Pratik değeri büyüktür. Sürükleme proble: Its practical value is great. The drag problem involves five variables (F, ρ, U, L, μ) and there are three fundamental dimensions (mass, length, time). 5 − 3 = 2 dimensionless numbers remain: C_D and Re. That is, instead of a five-dimensional experimental parameter sweep, plotting a single C_D(Re) curve is sufficient.
Pratik eşikler kabaca şöyledir: |CIN| <: Practical thresholds are roughly as follows: |CIN| < 25 J/kg means almost no cap, convection initiates easily; 25–100 J/kg is a moderate cap, a trigger is needed; above 100 J/kg is a strong cap, on most days convection does not initiate at all. But a cap is not entirely negative: a moderate cap allows energy to accumulate throughout the day and release all at once in the late afternoon, producing much more severe cells.
Pratik kullanım: ζ ve ∇·V alanları gözle: Practical use: the ζ and ∇·V fields are computed from observations, then two Poisson equations (∇²ψ = ζ and ∇²χ = ∇·V) are solved numerically. This is also the standard way of balancing the initial field in data assimilation.
Pratik kullanımı ölçüm kolaylığındandır:: Its practical use stems from ease of measurement: it is difficult to measure H and LE separately, whereas measuring temperature and humidity differences at two heights is easy. When turbulent transfer coefficients are assumed identical for both (similarity hypothesis), the ratio is obtained directly from gradients and combined with the energy budget to solve for both fluxes individually.
Pratik kural d ≈ 0,7·hᶜ (engel boyu). 20: Rule of thumb d ≈ 0.7·hᶜ (obstacle height). In a 20 m forest, d ≈ 14 m, z₀ ≈ 2 m; a measurement on a 20 m mast is actually effectively at only 6 m height.
Pratik kural şudur: bir dalga, ızgarada: The rule of thumb is: a wave requires at least 6–8 points to be resolved on a grid. "Effective resolution" is 5–7 times the grid spacing; a 3 km grid model reliably resolves not 3 km structures, but rather 15–20 km structures.
Pratik okumada yüzey haritasındaki basın: In practical reading, the pressure tendency symbol on the surface map (rising, falling, falling then rising) is among the earliest evidence of frontal passage; the tendency changes sign exactly as the front passes.
Pratik okuması çok güçlüdür: rüzgâr yüks: Its practical interpretation is very powerful: veering wind with height indicates warm advection, while backing wind indicates cold advection. The sign of advection is determined from a single radiosonde profile using this rule.
Pratik sonucu şudur: basınç eğilimini do: The practical consequence is: finding the pressure tendency directly via divergence calculation is numerically very sensitive, as it takes the difference of two large numbers. Therefore, the ω equation and vorticity advection are preferred in forecasting.
Pratik sonucu şudur: θe nin yükseklikle: The practical consequence is: a layer where θe decreases with height is potentially (convectively) unstable. If the layer is lifted as a whole, its lower portion saturates faster than its upper portion, destabilizing the profile. High θe at low levels and low θe at mid-levels is the classic severe storm signature.
Pratik sonuç şudur: 300 hPa'da diverjans: The practical consequence is: if there is divergence at 300 hPa, the air beneath is drawn upward, convergence occurs at the surface, and the low pressure deepens. Vertical motion is never an independent event; it is the result of mass conservation of the horizontal flow.
Pratik sonuç şudur: hava için tek bir µ: The practical consequence is: a single µ value is sufficient for air, and the stress-strain relationship is linear. This linearity is one of the few pieces of good news that allows the equations to be treated analytically — the remaining nonlinearity comes from the advection term.
Pratik sonuç: kirlilik, volkan külü ve t: Practical consequence: pollution, volcanic ash, and dust transport forecasts are made using trajectory models; rough estimates made from an instantaneous wind map turn out wrong due to system motion.
Pratik sonuç: sinoptik haritada izobar s: Practical consequence: the "geostrophic" speed read from isobar spacing on a synoptic map turns out LARGER than the real wind in cyclonic curvature, and SMALLER in anticyclonic curvature. You overestimate the wind at the center of a low, and underestimate it at the center of a high.
Pratik sınır kabaca 5–10 derecelik bir e: The practical limit is roughly a 5–10 degree latitude band; the f-plane is sufficient for mesoscale modeling, boundary layer studies, and the vicinity of a single storm, but not on a hemispheric scale.
Pratik sınır orta enlem sinoptik sisteml: The practical limit is approximately 10–15 days for mid-latitude synoptic systems. Beyond this, a single deterministic forecast is no better than a random scenario; meaningful information can only be provided statistically (climatologically or probabilistically).
Pratik tahmin: bulut tabanı yüksekliği ≈: Practical estimate: cloud base height ≈ 125 m × (T − Td). This Espy approximation works surprisingly well for convective clouds.
Pratik ölçüt: 3B sahneden alınan tek bir: Practical criterion: if a single screenshot taken from a 3D scene cannot answer the question without rotation, that scene is not suitable for a report. It may be valuable for interactive exploration, but a 2D cross-section belongs in printed output.

Radar ve lidar tamamen geri saçılma üzer: Radar and lidar are based entirely on backscattering: measuring the exact return of a small fraction of the transmitted energy.
Radar ve uydu tahminleri alansal örtü sa: Radar and satellite estimates provide spatial coverage but do not measure precipitation directly; they infer it indirectly from reflectivity or brightness temperature. Because of this delicate balance, it is difficult to forecast and is typically observed in valley bottoms.

SIK YAPILAN HATA: 3B‘yi etkileyici görün: COMMON MISTAKE: Choosing 3D because it looks impressive. In a 3D scene, the reader cannot compare two values (perspective distorts size), cannot see occluded data, and cannot read position. Most questions a meteorologist asks — “where is the gradient strong”, “at what time does the front pass”, “at how many meters is the inversion” — are answered in seconds on a well-prepared 2D cross section. Use 3D only when the question is truly three-dimensional: such as the angle an inclined frontal surface makes with the horizontal, or how the vertical axis of a supercell's rotating core tilts.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: 5 ve 10 numaralı durum: COMMON MISTAKE: Arbitrarily connecting cases 5 and 10 (two diagonal corners above, the other two below). This is the SADDLE case and has two valid solutions: are the two corners separate islands, or a diagonally connected neck. A wrong choice stitches low and high centers together, producing a ridge on the map that does not exist at all. Solution: estimate the value of the cell center from the average of the four corners and choose the connection accordingly.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: Web Mercator üzerinde: COMMON MISTAKE: Calculating area or average on Web Mercator. When you say “average precipitation in the box selected on screen”, the cells on the northern edge of the box represent a much smaller real area than those on the southern edge. Compute the average not on screen pixels, but on a geographic grid with cos(latitude) weighting.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: akım çizgisi ile YÖRÜN: COMMON MISTAKE: Confusing a streamline with a TRAJECTORY (trajectory). A streamline is tangent to the field of A SINGLE INSTANT; a trajectory is the path an air parcel actually follows over TIME. If the field changes with time, the two turn out completely different. While a streamline shows a neat spiral in a rapidly moving low center, the actual air parcel may have left the system long ago. When smoke plume or pollution transport is asked, the answer is trajectory, not streamline.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: animasyonda kareler ar: COMMON MISTAKE: Allowing the time interval between frames to change in an animation. Most models provide the first 48 hours in 1-hour steps and the remainder in 3-hour steps. If you play these frames at a constant rate, the system appears to SUDDENLY speed up threefold after hour 48. Scale the frame duration proportionally to the actual time interval, or indicate the transition point on screen.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: barb‘ı rüzgârın GİTTİĞ: COMMON MISTAKE: Assuming the barb indicates the direction the wind GOES. The barb and meteorological wind direction definition are based on the direction it COMES FROM; a “270-degree wind” is wind blowing from the west. In contrast, particle animations and streamlines flow in the direction it GOES. If both are on the same map, state this clearly to the reader.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: düşey abartmayı yazmad: COMMON MISTAKE: Publishing a convective cross section without specifying the vertical exaggeration. A thunderstorm plotted with VE = 100 appears 75 times steeper on screen, even though it is in reality a structure 15 km high and 20 km wide. The reader infers a “wall-like” cloud; however, the actual storm is wide and flat. Hiding the exaggeration is the same as hiding the scale bar.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: eş-yüzeyi tek bir eşik: COMMON MISTAKE: Drawing an isosurface with a single threshold and saying “this is the cloud's shape”. The isosurface is the shape of the selected threshold, not the object. Move the threshold by 20%, and the shell changes beyond recognition. An honest representation either displays multiple thresholds as nested semi-transparent layers or moves directly to volume rendering.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: görünmeyen katmanı çiz: COMMON MISTAKE: continuing to render a hidden layer. When the user switches tabs or a panel closes, particle animation continues rendering at 60 fps in the background in most engines. The battery drains, the device heats up, and no one sees anything. Every renderer must be behind a visibility gate.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: gözlem ile tahmini ayn: COMMON MISTAKE: plotting observation and forecast with the same line style. In a meteogram, the portion before the latest observation time is a measurement, while the portion after is an estimate; the two are epistemologically different. Make the distinction visually: observation as a thick solid line, forecast as a dashed line or low opacity; place a vertical “now” line between them. Failing to make this distinction presents something you didn't measure to the user as if you had measured it.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: haritada gördüğün ince: COMMON MISTAKE: confusing fine detail seen on a map with model resolution. If you see a 5 km wiggle on the screen and the model is on a 25 km grid, that wiggle is an artifact of interpolation. Memorize the rule: the smallest feature you can trust is about 6-8 grid spacings, not the pixel you see on the screen.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: her yakınlaştırma düze: COMMON MISTAKE: rendering the same detail at every zoom level. If you render all coastline nodes and wind arrows for every grid point at z = 3, the browser chokes, and nothing is distinguishable on the screen anyway. Scale-dependent generalization is mandatory: simplify geometry at small scales (using a method like Douglas-Peucker), widen arrow spacing, increase contour interval, filter out labels.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: iki-kübik ara değeri y: COMMON MISTAKE: applying bicubic interpolation to a precipitation field. The cubic kernel carries negative weights; in transitions from dry to wet areas, the result can be −0.4 mm. A physically impossible number leaks onto the map and breaks the lower end of the color scale. Use bilinear or conservative remapping for precipitation, and clamp the result at zero.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: ok uzunluğunu her kare: COMMON MISTAKE: normalizing arrow length to the domain maximum in each frame. In animation, the maximum changes frame by frame; consequently, when the wind weakens, the arrows LENGTHEN because the normalization baseline drops. The reader understands the exact opposite. The scale factor must be single and fixed across the entire time series.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: parçacıklara yaşam sür: COMMON MISTAKE: not giving particles a lifetime. Without a lifetime, all particles eventually accumulate in convergence zones; after a few seconds, most of the map is left completely empty, while a few streaks glow excessively. The user mistakes the empty region for “no wind” — whereas in reality, there are simply no particles left there.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: renkleri doğrudan sRGB: COMMON MISTAKE: blending colors directly with sRGB values. sRGB is non-linear, following a gamma curve of approximately 2.2. This is why two overlapping semi-transparent areas appear darker than expected. For physically accurate blending, first convert to linear space, blend, then convert back.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: rüzgâr yönünü sıralı b: COMMON MISTAKE: coloring wind direction with a sequential palette. 359° and 1° are nearly the same direction, but in a sequential palette, one maps to the darkest and the other to the lightest color; a sharp, completely artifactual boundary runs right through the north wind on the map. A CYCLIC palette is mandatory for direction.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: sürekli bir değişkeni: COMMON MISTAKE: encoding a continuous variable (temperature) into color HUE and expecting the reader to compare two regions. Hue is not ordered — the eye does not know whether orange is greater or less than purple; it only learns by checking the legend. In a continuous variable, **lightness** must increase monotonically; hue merely decorates.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: uyarıyı yalnızca renkl: COMMON MISTAKE: encoding warnings using color alone — “red area is dangerous, green area is safe”. Approximately one in sixteen men cannot distinguish between these two colors. Always add a second channel to color: a hatching pattern, a thick outline, a label, or an icon.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: yağış için eşit aralık: COMMON MISTAKE: using equally spaced contours for precipitation. If you divide 0-100 mm into 10 mm steps, you bury the difference between 2 mm and 8 mm — which is the most practically useful difference in daily life — inside a single interval. Use graduated (1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100) intervals for precipitation.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: yüksek çözünürlüklü ra: COMMON MISTAKE: downsampling a high-resolution radar raster by taking “every fourth pixel”. This is unfiltered subsampling; narrow precipitation bands fold into false broad bands and a moiré pattern appears on the screen. The correct way: first 4×4 area averaging (or Gaussian filtering), THEN decimation.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: “eksen her zaman sıfır: COMMON MISTAKE: blindly applying the rule “axes must always start from zero”. In an anomaly plot, zero MUST be on the axis because the sign is meaningful. In an absolute temperature plot, you do not have to start from 0 °C; showing the 18-24 °C range is legitimate. The decision depends on whether zero is a true reference for that variable.
SIK YAPILAN HATA: “jet renkli daha canlı: COMMON MISTAKE: defending jet by saying “jet is more vivid, it looks more appealing to students”. In a scientific map, appeal is not a metric. Plot the same field with jet and viridis, put the two outputs side by side: you will see that the sharp boundaries you see in jet do not exist in viridis. An inexistent boundary is the artifact of your palette.

Saçılma verimi dalga boyunun dördüncü ku: Scattering efficiency is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength. Blue light (450 nm) is scattered (650/450)⁴ ≈ 4.3 times more than red (650 nm); this is the quantitative reason why the sky appears blue.
Saçılmanın karakterini belirleyen büyükl: The quantity that determines the nature of scattering is the ratio of particle size to wavelength (size parameter x = 2πr/λ). If x ≪ 1, the Rayleigh regime applies; if x ≈ 1, Mie; and if x ≫ 1, the geometric optics regime applies.

Serbest atmosferde Ek çok küçüktür (10⁻⁴: In the free atmosphere, Ek is very small (order of 10⁻⁴) and friction is neglected; geostrophic balance works well. As the surface is approached, H decreases and Ek rises to order 1; this layer is precisely the Ekman layer.

Serbest atmosferde basınç gradyan kuvvet: In the free atmosphere, the pressure gradient force and Coriolis are in exact balance; the wind blows parallel to isobars/height contours (NH: low to the left).
Serbest atmosferde kesmenin kaynağı term: In the free atmosphere, the source of shear is the thermal wind, that is, the horizontal temperature gradient. In the boundary layer, the source is friction: velocity is near zero at the surface and increases rapidly along the logarithmic profile.

Ses hızı, basınç bozulmalarının ortamda: The speed of sound is the propagation speed of pressure perturbations in the medium. If the flow is slow compared to the speed of sound (Ma ≪ 1), pressure perturbations propagate much faster than the flow and density variations can be neglected; the flow can be solved as "incompressible". This is almost always true on meteorological scales.

Sirkülasyon alanla büyür, vortisite büyü: Circulation grows with area, vorticity does not. If you double the circle drawn around a cyclone, C quadruples, but ζ remains the same. Therefore, vorticity is used when comparing systems, while circulation is used when discussing the total rotational budget of a single system.

Sirkülasyon ile vortisite eşit sanılır;: Circulation is mistakenly assumed to be equal to vorticity; circulation is integrated over area, even their units are different.
Sirkülasyon makro, vortisite mikro: aynı: Circulation is macro, vorticity is micro: two scales of the same thing. The Bjerknes circulation theorem describes how circulation changes, while the vorticity equation describes how ζ changes; the two are related via Stokes' theorem.
Sirkülasyon r² ile büyür, alan da r² ile: Circulation grows with r², and area also grows with r²; when divided, the radius cancels out completely. The result is striking: in solid-body rotation, vorticity is INDEPENDENT OF POSITION and is exactly twice the angular velocity everywhere. The claim that vorticity is a "measure of local rotation" finds its numerical counterpart here.
Sirkülasyon ↔ vortisite: δC/δA = ζ ve St: Circulation ↔ vorticity: δC/δA = ζ and Stokes' theorem
Sirkülasyon, hız ile eğri elemanının çar: Circulation is the integral of the dot product of velocity and the curve element; when taking the derivative, BOTH depend on time. The first describes parcel acceleration (where the equation of motion enters), and the second describes the deformation of the curve itself — as the loop is advected with the flow, it stretches, shrinks, and twists. Ignoring the second term would mean treating the circuit as a rigid wire loop, which is incorrect.
Sirkülasyon, kapalı bir eğri boyunca teğ: Circulation is the integral of tangential velocity along a closed curve: a macroscopic measure of rotation. Vorticity, on the other hand, is point-wise. To connect the two, we take a small rectangle with sides δx, δy (counterclockwise circulation).
Sirkülasyon, kapalı yolun tamamı boyunca: Circulation is the integral taken along the entire closed path; for a rectangle, this reduces to the sum of contributions from all four sides. This line represents the closed form of the circuit — from here on, it is purely algebra, no new physics enters.
Sirkülasyon: kapalı bir eğri boyunca teğ: Circulation: the line integral of tangential velocity along a closed curve. It is the macroscopic, integral measure of rotation and depends on area.
Sirkülasyonu tanımlamak ve δx δy dikdört: Defining circulation and calculating it around a δx δy rectangle.
Sirkülasyonun hesaplandığı kapalı eğrini: The area enclosed by the closed curve over which circulation is computed. Because it appears in the denominator when transitioning to vorticity, it makes the result independent of area.
Sirkülasyonun maddesel türevini hareket: Writing the material derivative of circulation using the equation of motion.
Sirkülasyonun tanımı kapalı bir yol boyu: The definition of circulation is the sum of the velocity projected along a closed path. As the path, a "curvilinear rectangle" bounded by two adjacent streamlines separated by δn and two adjacent normals separated by δs is chosen. This is the natural coordinate counterpart of the flat rectangle in the Cartesian derivation (#60); the difference is that the edges are now arcs rather than straight lines.
Sirkülasyonun zaman değişimi solenoid in: The time rate of change of circulation reduces to the solenoidal integral; the angle between isobars and isotherms between warming land and cool sea establishes a closed circulation.
Sirkülasyonun zamanla değişimi Kelvin ve: The time variation of circulation is given by Kelvin's and Bjerknes' theorems; the baroclinic term is manifested here as the number of solenoids. Sea breeze, mountain-valley breeze, and frontal circulation are derived within this framework.

Skaler alana, o alanın en hızlı arttığı: An operator that assigns to a scalar field a vector field pointing in the direction of greatest increase of that field, with a magnitude equal to the rate of increase per unit length. It is everywhere perpendicular to constant-value surfaces (isotherms).
Skaler alanlar: dolgu, kontur, marching: Scalar fields: fill, contour, marching squares
Skaler alanın en hızlı arttığı yöne baka: A vector pointing in the direction of greatest increase of a scalar field, with a magnitude equal to that rate of increase. It is perpendicular to isolines; it grows as their density increases.
Skaler çarpım olduğu için yalnız rüzgârı: Because it is a dot product, only the component of the wind PERPENDICULAR to isolines does work. While a 40 m/s wind blowing parallel to isotherms produces zero temperature advection, an 8 m/s wind crossing isotherms perpendicularly produces strong advection. Su buharı kanalları (6,2 ve 7,3 μm) yüze: Water vapor channels (6.2 and 7.3 μm) never see the surface: the signal originates from moisture in the upper-to-middle troposphere. A low T_b indicates that the upper troposphere is moist, whereas a high T_b indicates that the signal comes from lower and warmer layers, meaning the upper levels are dry.
Su buharı molekül ağırlığı kuru havadan: Because the molecular weight of water vapor is smaller than that of dry air, moist air is lighter. A small addition is made to temperature in order to use the ideal gas law with the dry air constant.
Su buharı moleküllerinin havada derişim: The coefficient giving the rate of diffusion of water vapor molecules along a concentration gradient in air. It increases with temperature and decreases with pressure; it determines the first of the two resistances to diffusional growth.
Su buharı, doygunlukta bile ideal gaz gi: Water vapor behaves like an ideal gas even at saturation (e_s is small). When substituted for α_v, the differential form of Clausius–Clapeyron in meteorology emerges: the relative rate of increase of e_s is L_v/(R_v T²).
Su buharının kendi gaz sabiti; havanınki: Specific gas constant of water vapor; larger than that of air.
Su buharının üzerinde yoğuşabildiği, çoğ: Sub-micron aerosol particles, mostly hygroscopic, upon which water vapor can condense.
Su bütçesi kapanmıyorsa ya ölçümde hata: If the water budget does not close, there is either an error in measurement or groundwater exchange has been neglected.
Su bütçesi yoluyla dolaylı belirleme de: Indirect determination via the water budget is also possible: for a lake, inflow-outflow discharges and stage changes are measured, and the residual is evaporation. Error accumulation is high, but it is sufficient for long-term averages.

Virtual temperature resolves the issue by keeping the constant at the dry air value and assigning the correction to temperature: p = ρ Rd Tv.

Su yüzeyinin albedosu güneş açısına kuvv: The albedo of a water surface depends strongly on the solar elevation angle: while below 0.05 when the Sun is overhead, it rises above 0.3 at angles close to the horizon. One field in color, one field in lines — the eye does not confuse the two.

Vertical wind shear in the environment produces horizontal rotation; the updraft tilts this horizontal rotation into the vertical axis, creating a mesocyclone. Rotation keeps the updraft separate from precipitation, preventing the storm from choking itself; this is the secret to its long lifespan.

Süreç düşme hızı farkına dayanır: büyük: The process relies on terminal velocity differences: a large droplet falls faster, collecting smaller droplets ahead of it. If all droplets were the same size, relative velocity would be zero and collisions would never occur; this is why the width of the distribution is decisive.
Süreç izobariktir; adyabatik ıslak termo: The process is isobaric; the adiabatic wet-bulb temperature (θw) is very close to this, but not identical.
Süreç tamamen buzlu bulutta çalışmaz; he: The process does not operate in a completely glaciated cloud; both ice and supercooled water must coexist.
Süreç tersinir kabul edilir; karışma ve: The process is assumed to be reversible; mixing and friction are neglected.
Süreç, damlacık boyut dağılımının GENİŞL: The process leads to BROADENING of the droplet size distribution — the exact opposite of diffusion. The presence of a few large droplets in a cloud (e.g., from sea salt nuclei) significantly advances the onset of precipitation.

Sürtünme eklenirse: hız azalır ve akış i: If friction is added: speed decreases and flow crosses isobars toward low pressure.

Sürtünme kalktığı için basınç gradyan ku: Because friction is removed, the pressure gradient force and Coriolis force settle into balance; the wind blows roughly parallel to isobars. In the boundary layer, however, friction causes the wind to cross isobars, turning 10–30° toward low pressure.
Friction slows and deflects the wind.
Sürtünme sıfırlanırsa: akış tam jeostrof: If friction is set to zero: flow becomes purely geostrophic, flux toward low pressure and consequently convergence vanish.
Order of magnitude of the friction term: K·V/D².

Sürtünme yoksa dönme sermayesi harcanmaz: Without friction, rotational capital is not dissipated.
Sürtünme yüzünden yüzey rüzgârı izobarla: Due to friction, surface wind crosses isobars, deflecting toward low pressure. Conservation of mass forces this air upward — at the top of the boundary layer, w_E > 0.

Sürtünmeli tabakadaki konverjansın siklo: Convergence in the friction layer pumping vertical motion over the cyclone, gradually spinning down the system.

This equation rotates the direction of velocity at a constant rate without changing its magnitude: the result is an inertial circle traced clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere.

Sıcak (kırmızı) ve soğuk (mavi) alanları: Find the warm (red) and cold (blue) areas. The narrow transition zone between them is a candidate front.
Sıcak adveksiyon yükselişe, soğuk adveks: Warm advection is accompanied by ascent, and cold advection by subsidence. The reason is the balance condition: warm advection increases thickness, the column expands and bulges the height field aloft; to balance this, air rises. Most precipitation areas fall just poleward of the region where warm advection is maximized.
Sıcak cephe: ılık hava soğuğun üstüne tı: Warm front: warm air climbs over cold air, widespread precipitation
Sıcak cephenin \"sıcak getirdiği\" sanıl: It is assumed that a warm front "brings warmth"; surface temperature does not rise until the cold wedge erodes, and warming begins only after the front has fully passed.
Sıcak cephenin altındaki soğuk kama için: As precipitation falls into the cold wedge beneath the warm front, it evaporates, saturates the air, and produces prefrontal fog (precipitation fog) and freezing rain. In aviation, the warm front region is therefore one of the riskiest areas for icing.
Sıcak hava bir yanda, soğuk öbür yanda:: Warm air on one side, cold on the other: generates rotation.
Sıcak hava geniştir: aynı iki basınç ara: Warm air is expanded: thicker between the same two pressure levels.
Sıcak hava seyrektir: aynı pist uzunluğu: Warm air is less dense: the same runway length lifts less load on a hot day. The concept of density altitude reduces this to a single number; takeoff distance increases significantly at a high-elevation and hot aerodrome.
Sıcak hava solda kalacak şekilde eserse: If the wind blows with warm air on its left, the upper wind strengthens (Northern Hemisphere).
Sıcak hava çok daha fazla buhar taşır; h: Warm air holds much more vapor; doubling every 10 degrees.
Sıcak havanın soğuk hava kaması üzerine: A front with a gentle slope producing a widespread precipitation area, where warm air slowly climbs over a wedge of cold air.
Sıcak konveyör kuşağı (WCB) sıcak sektör: The warm conveyor belt (WCB) originates in the warm sector, ascends obliquely along the warm front, and turns anticyclonically away in the upper troposphere. This branch produces most of the cyclone's precipitation; the moisture flux it carries is comparable in magnitude to the discharge of a river.
Sıcak tarafta yüzeyler arası açılır: kal: On the warm side, the distance between surfaces expands: the thickness gradient gives rise to the thermal wind.
Sıcak ve soğuk hava yan yana geldiğinde: When warm and cold air lie side by side, rotation is generated.
Sıcak çekirdek yalıtımı tropikal siklonu: Warm-core seclusion is confused with the warm core of a tropical cyclone; the warming here comes from subsidence and its origin, not from latent heat release.
Sıcak çekirdekli antisiklon (Azor yükseğ: Warm-core anticyclones (Azores High, subtropical highs) are deep: they extend from the surface to the tropopause and strengthen with height. Their source is the descending branch of the Hadley cell and the warm column throughout the troposphere. This is the structure of summer heat waves.
Sıcak/soğuk dil (cephe) burada görünür —: The warm/cold tongue (front) is visible here — the advection shadow indicates the ADVANCEMENT direction of these tongues.
Sıcaklık 1 K düşerse doymuş pakette: faz: If temperature drops by 1 K in a saturated parcel: excess moisture condenses, latent heat is released, and cooling slows down (the origin of the moist lapse rate).

Sınır tabakada Ek = 0,10 (sürtünme Corio: In the boundary layer, Ek = 0.10 (friction is one-tenth of Coriolis, cannot be neglected); δ ≈ 316 m
Sınır tabakada PGF + Coriolis + sürtünme: In the boundary layer, PGF + Coriolis + friction are balanced; the wind veers with height (Ekman spiral) and crosses the isobars toward low pressure by ~10–45° at the surface → convergence into lows (Ekman pumping).
Sınır tabakada rüzgârı izobarlara 20–30°: It causes the wind in the boundary layer to cross the isobars at an angle of 20–30°; above 1 km its effect rapidly decays.
Sınır tabakada sürtünmeli rüzgâr, jeostr: In the boundary layer, frictional wind deviates from geostrophic by an angle; the cross-isobaric component is toward low pressure.
Sınır tabakada üç kuvvet dengededir: PGF: Three forces are in balance in the boundary layer: PGF, Coriolis, and friction (K ∂²V/∂z²).
Sınır tabakadaki sürtünme, siklonik döne: Friction in the boundary layer gathers air toward the center of a cyclonically rotating area and pumps this air upward; this is the mechanism by which low-pressure systems turn into clouds.
Sınır tabakanın en alt onda biri; akılar: The lowest tenth of the boundary layer; the layer where fluxes vary by less than 10% with height, and measurement and similarity laws are established.
Sınır tabakanın üstünde kalan, yüzey sür: The region above the boundary layer, where surface friction is neglected and the flow is nearly geostrophic.
Sınır tabakaya giren siklonlar bu terim: Cyclones entering the boundary layer weaken within a few days because of this term.
Sınır tabakayı üstteki serbest atmosferd: What separates the boundary layer from the free atmosphere above is turbulence: here, because air is in continuous and rapid exchange with the surface, momentum, heat, and moisture mix within minutes to hours. Above, transport is largely slow, stratified, and synoptic in scale.
Sınırda karekök sıfırdır: V = f|R|/2. Ay: At the limit, the square root is zero: V = f|R|/2. For the same gradient, the geostrophic wind is f|R|/4; thus the anticyclonic gradient wind is at most twice the geostrophic wind (Intermediate Step #21). This is the quantitative equivalent of the statement "wind around an anticyclone is supergeostrophic".
Sınırları da nettir. Cephe ölçeğinde (Ro: Its limits are also clear. At the frontal scale (Ro ~ 1), in convection, and in the tropics, QG breaks down. Today's models solve the primitive equations; QG is no longer a forecast engine, but the forecaster's language for interpreting physics: the sentence "warm advection produces ascent" is a QG statement.
Sınırları serttir: havza yaklaşık 2 km²: Its limitations are strict: the watershed must be smaller than approximately 2 km², precipitation must be assumed uniformly distributed over the area and of constant intensity, and there must be no storage (ponds, swamps). Therefore, it is used for sizing urban storm drains, culverts, and small bridges; in large basins, a unit hydrograph or hydrological model is required.
Sınırı açıktır: yoğuşma başladığı anda d: Its limit is clear: the moment condensation begins, the dq = 0 assumption breaks down because latent heat is released. Beyond that point (LCL), the parcel ascends along the moist adiabat.
Sınırı da nettir: model karasal ve yavaş: Its limit is also clear: the model explains continental and slowly developing cyclones well, but in rapidly deepening marine systems, the frontal structure behaves differently. There, frontal fracture and warm core isolation are observed; the model describing this is the Shapiro-Keyser model.
Sınırı yatay ölçektir. Yatay ölçek düşey: Its limit is the horizontal scale. When the horizontal scale becomes comparable to the vertical scale (convective cell, 1–10 km), vertical acceleration can no longer be neglected and non-hydrostatic models are required. This is why today's high-resolution models are non-hydrostatic.
Sınırı zamansal ve mekânsaldır: dünya ge: Its limitations are temporal and spatial: it is conducted twice daily worldwide at an average spacing of 300–500 km. Satellites, aircraft reports, and GNSS moisture data fill the gaps in between; however, there is still no measurement that fully replaces soundings in convective environment analysis.

Sırt altındaki çöküş, kalınlığı artırır: Subsidence under a ridge increases thickness and dries the layer; cloud formation is generally suppressed under a ridge. In summer, regions remaining within the 588 dam and higher contours at 500 hPa are candidates for heat waves.
Sırt ekseninde akış antisikloniktir, dol: Along the ridge axis, flow is anticyclonic, hence relative vorticity is negative. On the western flank of the ridge (transition from trough to ridge), there is negative vorticity advection and subsidence, while on the eastern flank (transition from ridge to trough), there is an upward motion tendency. Therefore, immediately ahead of and behind the ridge line produce different weather.
Sırtın ekseninde akış eğridir ama kesme: Along the ridge axis, flow is curved but shear is small (curvature dominates); at the edge of the jet core, flow is straight but shear is large (shear dominates).
Sırtın genliği akışın hızını yavaşlatır:: The amplitude of the ridge slows down the flow speed: as amplitude grows, systems track eastward more slowly; if it grows sufficiently, the flow breaks down and blocking begins.

TAF bir tahmindir, gözlem değildir; gene: A TAF is a forecast, not an observation; it is typically valid for 9, 24, or 30 hours.
TAF operasyonel bir karar aracıdır: alte: A TAF is an operational decision tool: alternate airport selection, contingency fuel calculation, and takeoff minimums are directly based on it. Teoremin bütün fiziksel içeriği bu ayrım: All the physical content of the theorem lies in this distinction. If density depends ONLY on pressure (barotropic), 1/ρ is also a function of p alone; then dp/ρ is an exact differential and integrates to zero over a closed path — absolute circulation is conserved, which is Kelvin's theorem. If density also depends on temperature (baroclinic), isobaric surfaces and isosteric (equal specific volume) surfaces INTERSECT; the "solenoids" formed in the intersection regions generate circulation. The atmosphere is always baroclinic; sea breezes, frontal circulations, and cyclogenesis are consequences of this.
Teoremin ifadesi basittir: n değişken ve: The statement of the theorem is simple: if there are n variables and k fundamental dimensions, the problem is completely defined by n − k dimensionless groups. A problem with five variables and three dimensions reduces to a single relationship between two dimensionless groups. The experimental burden is thus exponentially reduced.

Termal rüzgâr belli bir seviyedeki rüzgâ: Thermal wind is mistaken for a wind at a specific level; it is the DIFFERENCE between two levels and does not blow on its own.
Termal rüzgâr bir rüzgâr değil, bir kesm: Thermal wind is not a wind, but a shear vector: V_T = Vg(upper) − Vg(lower). It arises when the hypsometric equation is combined with geostrophic balance; because layer thickness is proportional to mean temperature, and thickness gradient is proportional to the wind difference.
Termal rüzgâr denklemi sıcaklık gradyanı: The thermal wind equation yields the temperature gradient; what we want is the inverse. Cross-multiplying both sides by k̂ and using the identity "k̂ × (k̂ × a) = −a" isolates the gradient. The minus sign comes from this identity and determines the sign of the result — if omitted, the veering/backing rule is reversed.
Termal rüzgâr denklemi ∇T̄ için çözülür: The thermal wind equation is solved for ∇T̄ (identity k̂ × k̂ × a = −a). Thus advection can be expressed using only two wind vectors: without measuring temperature, from the hodograph.
Termal rüzgâr denklemini sıcaklık gradya: Solve the thermal wind equation for the temperature gradient
Termal rüzgâr izotermlere paralel, sıcak: Thermal wind is parallel to isotherms, with warm air on the right. The layer-mean geostrophic wind V̄_g drives temperature advection as −V̄_g·∇T̄.
Termal rüzgâr izotermleri izler; sıcak s: Thermal wind follows isotherms; warm on the right (NH).
Termal rüzgâr ve kalınlıkla ilişkisi: Thermal wind and its relationship with thickness
Termal rüzgâr vektörü ile katman ortalam: Deducing the sign of temperature advection from the dot product of the thermal wind vector and the layer-mean wind.
Termal rüzgâr, katmanın ortalama sıcaklı: The thermal wind is perpendicular and proportional to the mean temperature gradient of the layer; in the NH, warm air remains on the right. It is the reason for the existence of the jet stream.
Termal rüzgâr: jeostrofik rüzgârın yükse: Thermal wind: variation of the geostrophic wind with height
Termal rüzgârı bir hodografta çizince, r: When plotting the thermal wind on a hodograph, the clockwise turning of the wind with height indicates warm air advection.
Termal rüzgârı gerçek bir rüzgâr sanmak:: Mistaking the thermal wind for an actual wind: it is a DIFFERENCE vector; upper wind = lower wind + thermal wind.

Termik: ısınan yüzeyden yükselen hava sü: Thermal: columns of air rising from the heated surface; summer afternoon, under cumulus.
Terminal hız eğrisi yarıçapa göre üç rej: Terminal velocity curve: three regimes according to radius.
Terminal hız yarıçapla hızla büyür: fark: Terminal velocity increases rapidly with radius: droplets of different sizes fall at different speeds; this difference is the engine of collision-coalescence.
Terminal hız: Stokes sürüklemesi ve daml: Terminal velocity: Stokes drag and droplet size
Termodinamik (mutlak) sıcaklık. Clausius: Thermodynamic (absolute) temperature. Because both its square appears in the denominator and its reciprocal in the exponential of the Clausius–Clapeyron relation, a shift in the zero of the scale renders the formula completely invalid.
Termodinamik dengede bir yüzey aldığı ka: In thermodynamic equilibrium, if a surface cannot return as much as it receives, it heats up or cools down; equilibrium is disrupted. This impossibility requires absorptivity and emissivity to be equal wavelength by wavelength. Here lies the power of the law: absorption is easy to measure, emission is difficult to measure; one gives the other.
Termodinamik enerji denklemi: bir noktan: Thermodynamic energy equation: why the temperature of a point changes
Termodinamik hesaplarda mutlak sıcaklık: Absolute temperature (Kelvin) is used in thermodynamic calculations: T(K) = T(°C) + 273,15. Using °C in formulas almost always yields incorrect results.
Ters V benzeri işaret türbülanstır; altı: An inverted V-like symbol indicates turbulence; the level range below it indicates the expected altitude. The one unrelated to clouds is clear-air turbulence (CAT) and does not appear on radar.
Ters basınç gradyanı altında yüzeye yakı: Deceleration and reversal of near-surface flow under an adverse pressure gradient, leading to separation from the surface.

Ters dönüşüm — teğetsel: birinciyi −sin: Inverse transformation — tangential: multiply the first by −sin θ, the second by cos θ, and add
Ters dönüşümün İKİNCİ satırı teğetsel bi: The SECOND row of the inverse transformation extracts the tangential component. This time the coefficients are −sin θ and +cos θ; when the grouped form of #41 is used on the left side, the RADIAL parcel is multiplied by zero and vanishes, while the tangential parcel survives. The pressure term comes from the second half of #45, and Coriolis comes from the same multiply-and-add.

The SECOND row of the inverse transformation extracts the tangential component; the coefficients this time are (−sin θ, +cos θ). Then (3.77) and (3.78) are again placed inside the brackets. No simplification is done at this step — the goal is to make visible which term will vanish in the next step.
Ters yön: 50 dBZ ölçülürse Z = 10⁵ → R =: Reverse direction: if 50 dBZ is measured, Z = 10⁵ → R = (10⁵/200)^0,625 = 500^0,625 = 48,6 mm/h
Ters yönde de kullanılır: kabul edilebil: It is also used in the reverse direction: acceptable risk is determined and the required T is calculated. For R = 10% and L = 50 years, T ≈ 475 years is obtained — this is the origin of that familiar number in earthquake codes.
Ters yönde, sıcak-nemli hava soğuk kara: In the opposite direction, when warm-moist air moves over cold land or cold sea, it cools from below, a near-surface inversion forms, vertical mixing ceases, and advection fog forms. The same air mass produces showers in one direction and fog in the opposite direction; the deciding factor is not the air mass, but the sign of the temperature difference between the air mass and the surface.
Tersi: 1 hPa düşüş ≈ 8,3 m tırmanışa kar: The inverse: a 1 hPa drop corresponds to ≈ 8,3 m climb.
Tersinme \"sıcak havanın üstte olması\"d: An inversion is "warm air being on top"; confusing this with the surface being warm reverses the stability interpretation.
Tersinme içinde θ yükseklikle hızla artt: Because θ increases rapidly with height within an inversion, a rising parcel immediately becomes colder than its surroundings and sinks back. This acts as an impermeable lid to turbulence; pollutants, moisture, and aerosols accumulate beneath it.
Tersinme kalınlığı 100–500 m · içinde +2: Inversion thickness 100–500 m · +2 to +10 K within · valley inversions can persist for days in winter
Tetikleyiciler ölçeklerine göre sıralanı: Triggers are classified by scale: synoptic (front, dryline, ascent ahead of a trough), mesoscale (sea breeze front, outflow boundary of a previous storm, mountain-valley circulation), and local (differential surface heating, orographic/hill forcing). Small-scale triggers are often invisible in models; therefore, satellite and radar monitoring is required.
Teğet birim vektöre dik, yatay düzlemde: Unit vector perpendicular to the tangent unit vector, lying in the horizontal plane and pointing to the left of the motion. Satisfies the relation t̂ × n̂ = k̂ by the right-hand rule; if the center of curvature is in the n̂ direction, the radius of curvature is considered positive.
Teğetsel bileşen için ters dönüşümün iki: Apply the second row of the inverse transformation for the tangential component
Teğetsel bileşen: hız şiddetinin denklem: Tangential component: equation of speed magnitude
Teğetsel bileşende 1/r çarpanını düşürme: Dropping the 1/r factor in the tangential component. Then the dimensions do not match and the growth of the force when approaching the center is lost.
Teğetsel bileşendeki 1/r çarpanı boyut d: The 1/r factor in the tangential component is an easy target for dimensional analysis: the unit of ∂p/∂θ is Pa/rad = Pa (radian is dimensionless); dividing by r gives Pa/m, dividing by ρ gives m s⁻². Even if the pressure difference per angle at the same radius is constant, as one approaches the center (as r decreases), the tangential force increases.
Teğetsel denklem, teğetsel hızın niçin d: The tangential equation tells why the tangential velocity changes. In a frictionless and circularly symmetric system (∂p/∂θ = 0, Fθ = 0), the right-hand side vanishes; the remaining expression is the starting point for the next proof, the conservation of angular momentum.
Teğetsel denklem: x'i −sin θ, y'yi +cos: Tangential equation: multiply x by −sin θ, y by +cos θ, and add
Teğetsel denklemde Coriolis teriminin iş: Mistaking the sign of the Coriolis term in the tangential equation to be the same as in the radial equation. Because the multipliers are (−sin, +cos), the sign flips: −2Ω sinφ Vθ in the radial equation, whereas +2Ω sinφ Vr appears in the tangential equation.
Teğetsel denklemden başlıyoruz ve düşey: We start from the tangential equation and drop the vertical-velocity Coriolis term — very small.
Teğetsel denklemi R ile çarpınca sol tar: Multiplying the tangential equation by R converts the left side into a single total derivative and the right side into the torque of the forces.
Teğetsel hareket denklemi, yarıçap R ola: The tangential equation of motion is written for a ring of radius R. In horizontal ring motion, the 2Ω cosφ w sinθ contribution is neglected; because the Coriolis term is moved to the left, its sign turns positive.
Teğetsel hareket denklemini mutlak açısa: Writing the tangential equation of motion as the time derivative of absolute angular momentum.
Teğetsel hız; gradyan rüzgâr dengesinin: Tangential velocity; the solved variable of gradient wind balance. Enters both centripetal and Coriolis terms in the radial equation.
Teğetsel hızın tanımı Vθ = r dθ/dt'dir;: The definition of tangential velocity is Vθ = r dθ/dt; by inverting it, a measurable quantity is substituted for dθ/dt. Without this substitution, the angular derivative would still remain in the result and the equation would not close.
Teğetsel paket (dVθ/dt + VrVθ/r) katsayı: Tangential parcel (dVθ/dt + VrVθ/r) is multiplied by the coefficient (+sin²θ + cos²θ) = 1 ⇒ remains unchanged.
Teğetsel sürtünme kuvveti; korunum koşul: Tangential friction force; the second pillar of the conservation condition is neglecting this. If friction exists, angular momentum decreases and the ring rotates slower than expected.
Thiessen ağırlıkları havza sınırı değişm: Thiessen weights are constant as long as the watershed boundary does not change; there is no need to redraw for every event, but all are updated when a station is added.
Thiessen yöntemi istasyon dağılımını dik: The Thiessen method takes station distribution into account but ignores terrain elevation. The isohyetal method, on the other hand, involves drawing isohyets and weighting the areas between two contours by the average value; it is the only realistic approach in mountainous basins where orographic precipitation dominates.

Tipleri damlacık boyutuna bağlıdır. Küçü: Their types depend on droplet size. Small droplets freeze upon impact and form porous, white "rime" accumulation. Large droplets spread over the surface and freeze; forming transparent, heavy "clear/glaze" ice that disrupts aerodynamics more severely. The most dangerous are supercooled large droplets (SLD, freezing drizzle); they spread aft of the area protected by anti-icing systems.

Toplayıcı damlanın birim zamanda süpürdü: Writing the mass of water swept out by the collector drop per unit time.
Toplayıcı damlanın büyüme hızı düşüş hız: The growth rate of the collector drop is proportional to its fall speed: unlike diffusion, it is an accelerating process and produces warm cloud rain in half an hour.
Toplayıcı damlanın geometrik kesitine gi: The fraction of small droplets entering the geometric cross-section of the collector drop that are actually captured and coalesce. It is the product of collision and coalescence efficiencies; it depends strongly on the size ratio of the droplet pair.

Toprak homojen ve başlangıç nemi düzgün: Soil is homogeneous and initial moisture is uniformly distributed.
Toprak kurursa: LE düşer, B büyür, maksi: If the soil dries: LE decreases, B increases, maximum temperature rises.

Toprak ve kayaç boşluklarını tamamen dol: Water completely filling soil and rock pores, under pressure in the saturated zone.
Toprak önceden ıslaksa: f₀ düşer, akış ç: If the soil is pre-wet: f₀ decreases, runoff begins much earlier, and total runoff increases.
Topraktan buharlaşma ile bitki terlemesi: The sum of evaporation from soil and transpiration from plants; the dominant component of water loss over land.
Toprağa giremeyen yağışın eğim boyunca a: The portion of precipitation that cannot infiltrate the soil, flows along the slope, and reaches the stream; it produces the peak of the flood hydrograph.
Toprağın su alma kapasitesi, yağmurun ba: The infiltration capacity of the soil decreases exponentially from the start of rainfall, approaching a constant lower limit.

Toz ve kum fırtınası, volkanik kül bulut: Dust and sand storm, volcanic ash cloud, tropical cyclone, radioactive cloud.
Transpoz: contourf(X, Y, Z) çağrısında Z: Transpose: in the contourf(X, Y, Z) call, the ROWS of Z must correspond to Y (latitude), and the columns to X (longitude).
Trigonometri radyan ister; derece bırakm: Trigonometry requires radians; leaving it in degrees makes the cos(φ) factor completely meaningless.
Tropikal bölgelerdeki sıcak yağmur sürec: The warm rain process in tropical regions operates entirely through this mechanism (without an ice phase).
Tropikal nem; bunaltıcı, şiddetli yağış: Tropical moisture; muggy, severe precipitation potential
Tropikal siklon oluşumunda alt seviyedek: In tropical cyclogenesis, low-level convergence contracts rings and produces cyclonic rotation; upper-level divergence expands rings and produces anticyclonic rotation — this is the anticyclonic outflow at the storm's top.
Tropikal siklonların ekvatorun ±5° kuşağ: This is one of the reasons why tropical cyclones cannot form within the ±5° belt of the equator.
Tropikal siklonun dış bölgesi serbest gi: The outer region of a tropical cyclone approximates a free vortex (Vθ ∝ 1/r), while its inner core behaves like a solid body — the transition between the two is at the eyewall.
Tropikal siklonun iç çekirdeği (göz duva: The inner core of a tropical cyclone (up to the eyewall) is close to this behavior; in the outer region, conversely, V ∝ 1/r.
Tropikal siklonun iç çekirdeği bu davran: The inner core of a tropical cyclone is close to this behavior; in the outer region, V ∝ 1/r and vorticity drops to nearly zero.
Tropiklerde 850–200 hPa yatay sıcaklık g: In the tropics, 850–200 hPa horizontal temperature gradient < 1 K/1000 km
Tropiklerde tablo değişir: Walker ve Had: In the tropics, the picture changes: the upper branch of the Walker and Hadley circulations is largely divergent, and the χ field directly indicates convection centers (including MJO phases). For this reason, streamline and velocity potential maps are used side by side in tropical analysis.
Tropopoz sabit bir yükseklik değildir; h: The tropopause is not a fixed altitude; it rises and sinks with the air mass.
Tropopoz yüksekliği enlemle değişir: ekv: Tropopause height varies with latitude: 16–18 km at the equator, 8–10 km at the poles. Jet streams are located in regions where tropopause breaks occur.
Tropopoz üstünde sıcaklık yükseklikle ar: Because temperature increases with height above the tropopause, the method completely breaks down there; structures such as overshooting tops are therefore recognized not by temperature, but by their relative cold pattern compared to their surroundings.
Tropopoz, sıcaklık düşüşünün durduğu sev: The tropopause is the level where temperature lapse stops; it appears on a cross-section as the height where the color scale begins to "invert" and slopes downward toward the pole.
Tropopoz: baklava biçimli kutularda uçuş: Tropopause: flight level in diamond-shaped boxes; H and L indicate local high and low points.
Troposfer 0,2–0,7 PVU · tropopoz 1,5–2 P: Troposphere 0.2–0.7 PVU · tropopause 1.5–2 PVU · stratosphere 4–10 PVU
Troposfer boyu bir kolon 10 km'dir; 2 km: A troposphere-deep column is 10 km; over a 2-km-high mountain range, it shrinks to 8 km.

Yasa Planck eğrisinin tepe noktasının ye: The law gives the position of the peak of the Planck curve. As an object warms, the peak shifts to shorter wavelengths; the transition from red hot to white hot metal is its everyday counterpart.
Yasa doğrusaldır ve düşük Reynolds sayıl: The law is linear and valid at low Reynolds numbers. In gravel pits or in the immediate vicinity of a well, flow may accelerate and linearity may break down; using Darcy in that region is incorrect.
Yasa toplam akı için geçerlidir; belirli: The law applies to total flux, not to a specific wavelength range. Because a satellite channel observes a narrow band, Planck's law itself is used there.
Yasa yalnız DOĞRUDAN demet için geçerlid: The law applies only to the DIRECT beam: photons that are scattered and change direction are outside the equation. Therefore, calculating total flux under cloudy skies with Beer–Lambert is incorrect, though it is valid for the direct component.
Yasa yalnız eylemsiz çerçevede bu biçimd: The law is valid in this form only in an inertial frame. The three terms on the right are real forces: only these genuinely push a parcel.
Yasa yalnız toplam akı için geçerlidir;: The law applies only to total flux; the Planck function dictates how much is emitted at each wavelength. The link between the two is an integral: integrating the Planck curve over all wavelengths yields σT⁴.
Yasa çok basit bir gözlemden çıkar: yolu: The law arises from a very simple observation: the energy lost in each small segment of the path is proportional to the intensity at that point. Integrating the proportionality coefficient along the path yields optical thickness τ, and attenuation is given by e^(−τ). τ = 1 means the path over which intensity decreases by a factor of e (about 63%).
Yasa üç durum değişkenini (p, ρ, T) birb: The law links the three state variables (p, ρ, T): without knowing one, the other two remain incomplete.
Yasa, laminer akış için geçerli bir doğr: The law is a linear relationship valid for laminar flow: doubling the gradient doubles the discharge. The minus sign indicates that water flows from higher head to lower head; flow is driven not by pressure, but by total hydraulic head (pressure + elevation). This distinction explains why artesian wells shoot upward.
Yasanın sınırı hızdır: çok yüksek eğimle: The limit of the law is velocity: at very high gradients or in coarse gravel, flow becomes turbulent (Re > 10) and linearity breaks down. At very low gradients, threshold behavior is observed in clay. In karstic media, flow resembles pipe flow; Darcy's law is not applicable at all.
Yasanın sınırı çoklu saçılmadır. Kalın b: The limit of the law is multiple scattering. In a thick cloud, a photon scatters multiple times and a portion still reaches the surface; simple exponential attenuation cannot account for this, requiring a two-stream or radiative transfer solution. Therefore, Beer–Lambert applies to the direct beam.

Yatay hareket denkleminin x ve y bileşen: Take the x and y components of the horizontal equation of motion.
Yatay hareket denklemlerinde dönmenin te: The only parameter of rotation in the horizontal equations of motion; it determines the geostrophic wind.

Yatay hız vektörüne her an paralel olan,: The unit direction vector, always parallel to the horizontal velocity vector, with a length equal to one. Its magnitude is constant, but when a parcel follows a curved path, its direction rotates along the path; therefore, its derivative is not zero.

Yatay momentum denklemi (sürtünmesiz). Ö: Horizontal momentum equation (frictionless). Scale analysis showed that acceleration is one-tenth of Coriolis; we drop it. The remaining two forces must balance each other.
Yatay momentum denklemindeki terimlerin: Estimating the order of magnitude of terms in the horizontal momentum equation using scales U, L, f, a.
Yatay momentum denklemlerine çapraz türe: Applying cross-differentiation to the horizontal momentum equations to derive the material rate of change of ζ.
Yatay olarak homojen yüzey; yanal adveks: Horizontally homogeneous surface; lateral advection is neglected.

Yöntem basittir: T_b alınır, aynı bölgey: The method is simple: T_b is taken, the level where this value occurs in the radiosonde or model temperature profile for the same region is located, and the altitude of that level is taken as the cloud top. The assumption works well for convective clouds because their tops are optically thick.
Yöntem basittir: n yıllık kayıttaki yıll: The method is simple: the annual maximum discharges in an n-year record are ranked from largest to smallest, and each is assigned a rank number m. For the largest value (m = 1), T = n + 1 is obtained. Adding 1 to the denominator (Weibull plotting position) is intended to reduce bias in finite records.
Yöntem model içermez: 10–20 Hz'lik sonik: The method involves no model: the covariance of 10–20 Hz sonic anemometer and gas analyzer measurements is the direct flux. Therefore, it serves as the reference for all other flux methods.
Yöntem üç adımlıdır: görüntüde izlenebil: The method consists of three steps: a trackable target is selected in the image, the same pattern is sought in the next image, and velocity is found by dividing displacement by time. Then, a height is assigned to the target; this assignment is usually made via T_b and is the weakest link in the process.
Yöntemin cazibesi doğrudanlığıdır: denkl: The appeal of the method lies in its directness: discretizing the equation takes only a few lines, the code is simple, and the order of error is read from the Taylor series expansion. This is why most atmospheric models, especially in the vertical, use finite differences.
Yöntemin en zayıf olduğu durum yağmurun: The method is weakest when rain falls on snow: rain both carries heat and disrupts the snowpack structure, causing melting much faster than predicted by temperature alone. Many major spring floods are caused by this mechanism.
Yöntemin gücü, tek bir istasyonun tek bi: The power of the method lies in its ability to diagnose advection from a single sounding of a single station: no map, neighboring station, or model is needed. This was the backbone of pre-satellite frontal analysis and remains a quick verification tool today.
Yöntemin mantığı basittir: yağış havzanı: The rationale of the method is simple: if precipitation lasts as long as the basin's time of concentration, the entire basin contributes to the outlet simultaneously and discharge peaks. Therefore, the rainfall intensity to be used is the intensity for duration tc at the selected return period, not the daily total precipitation.
Yöntemin sınırı şudur: hangi değişkenler: The limitation of the method is this: it does not tell you which variables are important. If you formulate the physics incompletely and omit a variable, the analysis will silently yield incorrect results. Furthermore, it does not provide the functional relationship connecting the groups; that is determined by experiment or theory.
Yöntemin zayıf noktası hata birikimidir:: The weak point of the method is error accumulation: ω is the vertical integral of divergence, and divergence is calculated as the small difference between two large numbers. A 5% error in wind measurement can reach 50% in divergence and accumulates through the integral. For this reason, a correction is made in practice using the upper boundary condition (ω = 0).
Yöntemin zayıf noktası, B nin −1 e yakla: The weak point of the method occurs when B approaches −1: because (1 + B) in the denominator approaches zero, the solution blows up. This happens during dawn and dusk transitions, and values during those hours should be filtered out.
Yöntemler arasındaki fark küçümsenmemeli: The difference between methods should not be underestimated: in a mountainous catchment, a deviation exceeding 30% between arithmetic mean and isohyetal results is common, directly affecting flood calculations.

Yörüngenin yerel eğrilik yarıçapı; siklo: Local radius of curvature of the trajectory; signed positive for cyclonic curvature and negative for anticyclonic curvature. It determines the magnitude of centripetal acceleration as V²/R and dictates which root of the equation is physical.
Yörüngenin yönü sistemin nereye gideceği: The direction of the trajectory indicates where the system is heading; speed is written in km/h on the center card.
Yörüngeye dik doğrultuda kuvvet dengesi: Write the force balance perpendicular to the trajectory: PGF + Coriolis = centripetal acceleration.
Yörüngeye dik normal eksen boyunca basın: Pressure gradient along the normal axis perpendicular to the trajectory. On the cyclostrophic scale, it reaches thousands of times synoptic values; the square of the velocity is directly proportional to this gradient.
Yörüngeye o noktada en iyi uyan çemberin: The radius of the osculating circle at that point. Its sign is taken as positive if the center of curvature is in the n̂ direction (to the left); in straight flow, it approaches infinity and the centripetal term vanishes.

Yükselen bulut, çevresindeki havayı yanl: The rising cloud entrains ambient air from its sides and top. The entrained air is dry and has a lower potential temperature; it evaporates some of the cloud droplets, which cools the air further and reduces buoyancy.
Yükselen bulutta üretilir, damlalar tüke: Produced in the rising cloud, consumed by droplets.
Yükselen hava genişler, genişleyen hava: Rising air expands, expanding air cools: 10 degrees per km.
